data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 offers a process-level rationales test as the single-evaluation evidence distinguishing genuine reliability from mere checklist compliance, but its own countercondition concedes that for purely perceptual tasks (e.g., identifying a tumor in an MRI) there may be no decomposable rationale to verify. The problem asks broadly about 'tasks with objectively verifiable outcomes,' which plainly includes perceptual verification tasks. Thus the proposed if-and-only-if criterion fails: a single evaluation can distinguish genuine gain on tasks with decomposable rationales, but on perceptual tasks the criterion admits it has no applicable mechanism, so the claimed iff test is not actually general to the class of objectively verifiable tasks the problem concerns.
